digest.component_or_area: plan review sizing / model escalation ladder
propositions: When a plan review hits a provider context limit and no model-class table is configured, the escalation path silently relocates the call from a provider-qualified model (e.g. Bedrock) to a bare Anthropic model id, causing unbudgeted spend or hard failures in provider-isolated containers.

The _rung_target function compares rung class resolution against inferred provider but never receives the run's actual primary model as input, so it cannot detect provider mismatches between the run's model and the escalation target.

A Bedrock-qualified primary model like bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8-v1:0 with no class table configured produces bare model names like claude-opus-4-8 during escalation, which are not valid Bedrock model ids when composed with cfg.model_provider.
The models_at_or_above function must thread the run's primary model into _rung_target so that provider agreement can be enforced and unnameable higher rungs can be dropped rather than crossed.

Escalation targets for Anthropic-qualified or unqualified primaries must preserve today's byte-for-byte bare form for back-compatibility while preventing silent provider transitions when providers differ.
The fix applies only to the located-start-rung branch and must not change the window lookup mechanism or the no-match fallback behavior.
